goal: Projects that depend on zig-mime stop downloading zig-bench: the benchmark dependency is fetched only when someone asks for benchmarks.
scope: A `-Dbench` build option, off by default, that guards the `lazyDependency("bench")` call
The `bench` step says to pass `-Dbench` when the option is off
README and CI updated to pass the option wherever benchmarks run
notes: A lazy dependency is still requested whenever the build script runs, including when zig-mime is only a dependency, so the call itself has to be conditional
Found in mail-os/mail#23: every fresh mail build began fetching zig-bench 0.2.1
accept: A project that depends on zig-mime builds from an empty cache without fetching zig-bench
`zig build bench -Dbench` still runs the benchmarks
Released as a patch version, and mail's build.zig.zon updated to it

goal: The spam filter reads base64 MIME parts the way the rest of the server parses mail, so a pitch hidden in a bare-LF or folded-header part is decoded and scored.
scope: Feed the scan window to zig-mime's walker and decode base64 and quoted-printable text parts into the phrase scan buffer
Keep the existing scan window and output bounds
accept: Tests show a base64 text/html part is decoded when its headers use bare LF, folded `Content-Transfer-Encoding`, or mixed case, and each fails on the old code
Every existing spam filter test passes
`zig build test`, `zig build test-rfc`, `zig build test-fuzz` and `zig build test-e2e` pass
notes: decodeBase64Parts searches the scan window for a Content-Transfer-Encoding line by hand, so header folding and bare-LF framing hide the part
src/message/mime.zig is the zig-mime adapter from P12.06

goal: Webmail shows the same parts and attachments the scanner sees: its message view and inline images parse multipart bodies with zig-mime.
scope: Move webmail_maildir's body and attachment extraction onto zig-mime, keeping the `BodyParts` shape its callers use
Move inline image extraction onto zig-mime, including Content-ID lookup
Use zig-mime's RFC 2047 and RFC 2231 decoding for filenames and subjects where webmail decodes them by hand
Delete the replaced helpers once nothing uses them
out_of_scope: Composing outgoing multipart mail (webmail_compose.zig), which writes MIME rather than parsing it
accept: A bare-LF multipart message shows the same parts and attachments in webmail as its CRLF form, with a test that fails on the old code
`zig build test`, `zig build test-rfc`, `zig build test-fuzz` and `zig build test-e2e` pass
notes: webmail_maildir.zig splits bodies in parseMultipart, parseMultipartMode and extractBoundary, and decodes encoded words in decodeMimeWords
inline_images.zig finds the boundary with findBoundary; src/api/webmail.zig uses it

goal: IMAP clients see the message structure the scanner sees: BODYSTRUCTURE and BODY[section] come from zig-mime's part tree.
scope: Build BODYSTRUCTURE from zig-mime's nested parts: type, subtype, parameters, id, description, encoding, size and lines, extension data where cheap
Serve BODY[n.m] section fetches from the same part offsets
Bound the work by zig-mime's depth and part limits, and fall back to a single text part when a limit is hit
out_of_scope: Other FETCH items and IMAP extensions
accept: Tests compare BODYSTRUCTURE for nested multipart, message/rfc822 and bare-LF messages against expected strings
A real client lists the attachments of a nested multipart message
`zig build test`, `zig build test-rfc`, `zig build test-fuzz` and `zig build test-e2e` pass
notes: The FETCH handler builds BODYSTRUCTURE by sniffing the top-level Content-Type, so nested parts are not described
